title: Recovery Gate: ephemeral probing and soft fallback paths for latency surges
author: Aisha Raman
release_notes: Adds a conservative recovery gate that performs short ephemeral probes before fully re-enabling traffic to a previously degraded region; introduces a feature flag and telemetry to observe reopen attempts. Backwards compatible; can be disabled via runtime flag.
description:
Motivation: During the 2026-02-07 latency surge we observed tight quarantine semantics coupled with immediate reopen attempts that caused oscillation and prolonged regional instability. This change introduces a 'recovery gate' that performs ephemeral probes to validate capacity and responsiveness before restoring normal traffic, plus a soft fallback path that gradually increases traffic instead of a hard switch.

Design summary: single gate component in the serving runtime that: (1) marks a region/queue in a candidate 'recovery' state after a circuit-close event, (2) issues time-boxed probe requests with synthetic low-cost load to verify tail latency and token-throughput, (3) applies a staged ramp (10% -> 30% -> 60% -> 100%) with health checks at each step, and (4) falls back to a soft-pass-through policy when probes are inconclusive. Implementation includes a feature-flagged controller, metric hooks, and a conservative default timeout/hysteresis.

Why this is different: previous approaches re-enabled traffic based on a single probe or time-based window. The recovery gate performs multiple ephemeral probes with heuristics that account for cold-KV-warmup and transient GC spikes, reducing premature reopen-induced oscillation.

Testing and rollout: unit tests for probe state machine and hysteresis; integration tests simulating delayed KV loads and spike patterns; a canary pipeline that routes 2% traffic and a staged rollout script. The change is behind feature flag 'recovery_gate.v1' and will be enabled in canary for 72 hours before wider rollout.

Checklist: [x] unit tests added, [x] integration tests added, [x] load-sim harness updated, [x] feature flag gated, [x] observability metrics and dashboards updated, [x] canary pipeline configured.

Files changed (high level): added recovery gate controller, probe harness, metric labels, config knobs, canary pipeline manifest, tests. See changed_files for specifics.

Impact: expected to reduce reopen oscillations and lower repeated-degradation events by avoiding single-probe reopens. Slight increase in control-plane calls for probing (configurable).

Operational notes: Ops runbook updated with commands to force-open / force-close the gate and to view probe history per region.

Author: We implemented soft-drop semantics: mid-ramp degradation triggers a controlled deceleration and re-run of an ephemeral probe; only after two consecutive failed steps do we revert to quarantine. Documented in runbook.

Author: Increased timeouts and reran CI.
Diego: Code LGTM after addressing comments. Helen approved with minor nits. Samir approved after confirming runbook steps.

risk_assessment: low-medium: changes are feature-flag guarded and additive. Probe traffic is synthetic and throttled by default. Primary risk is insufficient probe coverage for rare failure modes; mitigated by staged canary and monitoring alerts.
notes: Initial canary ran for 72h with no reopen oscillations observed in the monitored cohorts; metrics show 42 probe attempts and 36 successful ramps in canary. Will schedule cross-team review after wider rollout.
